Hi Eve — adding some technical detail for the matrix (summary):

1) Categories of transfer scenarios we mapped:
   - API request processing (short-lived request tokens, transient KV cache)
   - Long-term embedding storage for product features (customer dataset storage)
   - Batch analytics (customer-initiated batch jobs)

2) Technical measures (examples):
   - Transport encryption: TLS1.3 mandatory between client and frontends; mutual TLS for private endpoints. Evidence: load balancer config + cert rotation logs (available).
   - Data at rest: AES-256 encryption in our object stores. Evidence: storage policy screenshots + KMS CMK metadata.
   - KMS model: Hosted = Redwood-managed CMKs; Dedicated/Private = optional customer-managed CMKs (BYOK). Evidence: kms_keyflow.pdf (diagram) + sample CloudTrail key-usage log extract.
   - KV/prefix caching: TTLs are configurable per-tenant; default short TTL for prompt contexts to reduce export surface. Evidence: config snippet included.
   - Access control: RBAC + time-limited developer keys + token rotation; evidence: IAM role list export (sanitized).

3) Residual risk notes (high level):
   - Hosted customers relying on Redwood-managed keys accept operational key access for emergency/key-rotation operations. We flag this in the matrix and provide mitigations (audit logs, attested key-usage, limited-privilege escalation).
   - Cross-region replication: some models and caches may replicate for latency; we can pin model variants to region-only deployment when required.

I attached the initial matrix and a compact KMS keyflow PDF. There are placeholders where we will insert sanitized log extracts if NexonCare confirms NDA+transfer authorization.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: transfer_control_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: kms_keyflow.pdf (pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Eve Martin <eve.martin@nexoncare.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: control evidence for cross-border processing (NexonCare)

Hi Eve — attaching a short DPA Annex draft tailored to the scenarios Marissa outlined. Key legal points:

- Contractual basis and flow-down to subprocessors (we propose a regional routing clause and an explicit subprocessor list by function).
- KMS: options for BYOK / customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private; hosted customers receive cryptographically-separated CMKs under Redwood control but with audit capability.
- Audit/evidence: we commit to share SOC-2 Type II report reference and scoped key-use logs on a limited-sampling basis via an NDA addendum; we can also provide a redacted configuration snapshot for procurement review.
- Data subject requests & retention: retention defaults and deletion runbook are included as an appendix reference.

If NexonCare legal wants the Annex to reference EU DPF-specific terminology or include supplementary technical annex pages, note which terms you prefer (DPF / SCC / EU Standard Contractual Clauses / new adequacy frameworks).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
